tone_statements.citation: Lotven, Samson. 2023. Tone in South Central Tibeto-Burman. Himalayan Linguistics 22(1): 36-66. Santa Barbara: eScholarship, University of California.
tone_statements.quote: in Zotung, a language with only CVV and CVʔ syllables, the underlying H vs. L contrast is realized as Convex [454] vs. Falling [42] on CVV syllables, but as High [55] vs. Low-Falling [31] on CVʔ syllables, when not neutralized (Shintani 2015: xxi). ... In Zotung, for example, all tonal contrasts and contours are limited to occurring “at the end of a semantic junction” and are neutralized elsewhere to a “slightly rising rhythm” (Shintani 2015: xviii). ... [fn. 12] The only Maraic language as yet described without three pitch levels is Zotung, which has two level tones (H and M) as well as a ML contour (Shintani 2015: xxi).

sources.citation: Lotven, Samson Alexander. 2021. The Sound Systems of Zophei Dialects and Other Maraic Languages. PhD dissertation, Indiana University, Bloomington. 437 pp. hdl.handle.net/2022/27043 (open).
sources.quote: p.33: 'Zotung makes use of a two-way lexical tone contrast realized as High-Rising-Falling [454] vs. Falling [42] in open syllables and High Level [55] vs. Low-Falling [31] in syllables closed with a glottal stop. Shintani (2015) notes that this contrast is only "at the end of a semantic junction" and is neutralized to a "slightly rising rhythm" elsewhere. Some grammatical particles are analyzed as having "no inherent tone" and usually surface as Mid-Level [33].' fn.7: 'Though Shintani reports no minor syllables in Zotung, he does report some words with initial vowels with no inherent tone, su

sources.note: Open, page-cited summary of Shintani 2015's Zotung tone analysis (Sec. 2.4 p.33; 6.3.1 p.221; 6.5 p.236-7): two-way lexical tone H vs L with syllable-type-conditioned realizations, neutralized non-finally. Should replace VanBik-2009-apud-Luce as the deciding citation.

sources.note: The sole primary description of Zotung; its introduction (p. xxi per Lotven 2021) states the tone system (two tones, contrast only phrase-finally, toneless particles) and syllable canon. Our record quotes it only second-hand and no held text gives Shintani's own wording on tone or on any stress/rhythm ('slightly rising rhythm').
